content.text:
1	---
     2	name: docx
     3	description: "Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation."
     4	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     5	---
     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `extract-text`, or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction as markdown
    33	extract-text document.docx
    34	
    35	# Show tracked changes instead of accepting them
    36	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    37	
    38	# Raw XML access
    39	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    40	```
    41	
    42	### Converting to Images
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    46	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    47	```
    48	
    49	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    50	
    51	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    52	
    53	```bash
    54	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    55	```
    56	
    57	---
    58	
    59	## Creating New Documents
    60	
    61	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    62	
    63	### Setup
    64	```javascript
    65	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    66	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    67	        InternalHyperlink, Bookmark, FootnoteReferenceRun, PositionalTab,
    68	        PositionalTabAlignment, PositionalTabRelativeTo, PositionalTabLeader,
    69	        TabStopType, TabStopPosition, Column, SectionType,
    70	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    71	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    72	
    73	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    74	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    75	```
    76	
    77	### Validation
    78	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    79	```bash
    80	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    81	```
    82	
    83	### Page Size
    84	
    85	```javascript
    86	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    87	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    88	sections: [{
    89	  properties: {
    90	    page: {
    91	      size: {
    92	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    93	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    94	      },
    95	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    96	    }
    97	  },
    98	  children: [/* content */]
    99	}]
   100	```
   101	
   102	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
   103	
   104	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
   105	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   106	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   107	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   108	
   109	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   110	```javascript
   111	size: {
   112	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   113	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   114	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   115	},
   116	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   117	```
   118	
   119	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
   120	
   121	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   122	
   123	```javascript
   124	const doc = new Document({
   125	  styles: {
   126	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   127	    paragraphStyles: [
   128	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   129	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   130	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   131	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   132	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   133	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   134	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   135	    ]
   136	  },
   137	  sections: [{
   138	    children: [
   139	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   140	    ]
   141	  }]
   142	});
   143	```
   144	
   145	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   146	
   147	```javascript
   148	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   149	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   150	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   151	
   152	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET
   153	const doc = new Document({
   154	  numbering: {
   155	    config: [
   156	      { reference: "bullets",
   157	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   158	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   159	      { reference: "numbers",
   160	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   161	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   162	    ]
   163	  },
   164	  sections: [{
   165	    children: [
   166	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   167	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   168	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   169	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   170	    ]
   171	  }]
   172	});
   173	
   174	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   175	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)
   176	// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)
   177	```
   178	
   179	### Tables
   180	
   181	**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.
   182	
   183	```javascript
   184	// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering
   185	// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds
   186	const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: "CCCCCC" };
   187	const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
   188	
   189	new Table({
   190	  width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Always use DXA (percentages break in Google Docs)
   191	  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Must sum to table width (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)
   192	  rows: [
   193	    new TableRow({
   194	      children: [
   195	        new TableCell({
   196	          borders,
   197	          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell
   198	          shading: { fill: "D5E8F0", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID
   199	          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)
   200	          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Cell")] })]
   201	        })
   202	      ]
   203	    })
   204	  ]
   205	})
   206	```
   207	
   208	**Table width calculation:**
   209	
   210	Always use `WidthType.DXA` — `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` breaks in Google Docs.
   211	
   212	```javascript
   213	// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width
   214	// US Letter with 1" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA
   215	width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },
	< truncated lines 216-378 >
   379	```
   380	
   381	### Critical Rules for docx-js
   382	
   383	- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents
   384	- **Landscape: pass portrait dimensions** - docx-js swaps width/height internally; pass short edge as `width`, long edge as `height`, and set `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE`
   385	- **Never use `\n`** - use separate Paragraph elements
   386	- **Never use unicode bullets** - use `LevelFormat.BULLET` with numbering config
   387	- **PageBreak must be in Paragraph** - standalone creates invalid XML
   388	- **ImageRun requires `type`** - always specify png/jpg/etc
   389	- **Always set table `width` with DXA** - never use `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` (breaks in Google Docs)
   390	- **Tables need dual widths** - `columnWidths` array AND cell `width`, both must match
   391	- **Table width = sum of columnWidths** - for DXA, ensure they add up exactly
   392	- **Always add cell margins** - use `margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }` for readable padding
   393	- **Use `ShadingType.CLEAR`** - never SOLID for table shading
   394	- **Never use tables as dividers/rules** - cells have minimum height and render as empty boxes (including in headers/footers); use `border: { bottom: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6, color: "2E75B6", space: 1 } }` on a Paragraph instead. For two-column footers, use tab stops (see Tab Stops section), not tables
   395	- **TOC requires HeadingLevel only** - no custom styles on heading paragraphs
   396	- **Override built-in styles** - use exact IDs: "Heading1", "Heading2", etc.
   397	- **Include `outlineLevel`** - required for TOC (0 for H1, 1 for H2, etc.)
   398	
   399	---
   400	
   401	## Editing Existing Documents
   402	
   403	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   404	
   405	### Step 1: Unpack
   406	```bash
   407	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   408	```
   409	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   410	
   411	### Step 2: Edit XML
   412	
   413	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   414	
   415	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   416	
   417	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   418	
   419	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   420	```xml
   421	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   422	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>
   423	```
   424	| Entity | Character |
   425	|--------|-----------|
   426	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   427	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   428	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   429	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   430	
   431	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   432	```bash
   433	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   434	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   435	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   436	```
   437	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   438	
   439	### Step 3: Pack
   440	```bash
   441	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   442	```
   443	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   444	
   445	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   446	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   447	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   448	
   449	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   450	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   451	
   452	### Common Pitfalls
   453	
   454	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   455	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   456	
   457	---
   458	
   459	## XML Reference
   460	
   461	### Schema Compliance
   462	
   463	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   464	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   465	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   466	
   467	### Tracked Changes
   468	
   469	**Insertion:**
   470	```xml
   471	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   472	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   473	</w:ins>
   474	```
   475	
   476	**Deletion:**
   477	```xml
   478	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   479	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   480	</w:del>
   481	```
   482	
   483	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   484	
   485	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   486	```xml
   487	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   488	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   489	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   490	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   491	</w:del>
   492	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   493	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   494	</w:ins>
   495	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   496	```
   497	
   498	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   499	```xml
   500	<w:p>
   501	  <w:pPr>
   502	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   503	    <w:rPr>
   504	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   505	    </w:rPr>
   506	  </w:pPr>
   507	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   508	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   509	  </w:del>
   510	</w:p>
   511	```
   512	Without the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.
   513	
   514	**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:
   515	```xml
   516	<w:ins w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   517	  <w:del w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   518	    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>
   519	  </w:del>
   520	</w:ins>
   521	```
   522	
   523	**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):
   524	```xml
   525	<w:del w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   526	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   527	</w:del>
   528	<w:ins w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   529	  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>
   530	</w:ins>
   531	```
   532	
   533	### Comments
   534	
   535	After running `comment.py` (see Step 2), add markers to document.xml. For replies, use `--parent` flag and nest markers inside the parent's.
   536	
   537	**CRITICAL: `<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` are siblings of `<w:r>`, never inside `<w:r>`.**
   538	
   539	```xml
   540	<!-- Comment markers are direct children of w:p, never inside w:r -->
   541	<w:commentRangeStart w:id="0"/>
   542	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   543	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted</w:delText></w:r>
   544	</w:del>
   545	<w:r><w:t> more text</w:t></w:r>
   546	<w:commentRangeEnd w:id="0"/>
   547	<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="CommentReference"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id="0"/></w:r>
   548	
   549	<!-- Comment 0 with reply 1 nested inside -->
   550	<w:commentRangeStart w:id="0"/>
   551	  <w:commentRangeStart w:id="1"/>
   552	  <w:r><w:t>text</w:t></w:r>
   553	  <w:commentRangeEnd w:id="1"/>
   554	<w:commentRangeEnd w:id="0"/>
   555	<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="CommentReference"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id="0"/></w:r>
   556	<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="CommentReference"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id="1"/></w:r>
   557	```
   558	
   559	### Images
   560	
   561	1. Add image file to `word/media/`
   562	2. Add relationship to `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`:
   563	```xml
   564	<Relationship Id="rId5" Type=".../image" Target="media/image1.png"/>
   565	```
   566	3. Add content type to `[Content_Types].xml`:
   567	```xml
   568	<Default Extension="png" ContentType="image/png"/>
   569	```
   570	4. Reference in document.xml:
   571	```xml
   572	<w:drawing>
   573	  <wp:inline>
   574	    <wp:extent cx="914400" cy="914400"/>  <!-- EMUs: 914400 = 1 inch -->
   575	    <a:graphic>
   576	      <a:graphicData uri=".../picture">
   577	        <pic:pic>
   578	          <pic:blipFill><a:blip r:embed="rId5"/></pic:blipFill>
   579	        </pic:pic>
   580	      </a:graphicData>
   581	    </a:graphic>
   582	  </wp:inline>
   583	</w:drawing>
   584	```
   585	
   586	---
   587	
   588	## Dependencies
   589	
   590	- **pandoc**: Text extraction
   591	- **docx**: `npm install -g docx` (new documents)
   592	- **LibreOffice**: PDF conversion (auto-configured for sandboxed environments via `scripts/office/soffice.py`)
   593	- **Poppler**: `pdftoppm` for images

input.file_text:
The Thessalonian Mandate Institute
Austin, Texas  ·  EIN 42-2419586  ·  26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A)
Lease Agreement
1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Lee County, Texas 78942

This Lease Agreement (hereinafter "Lease") is entered into as of the day of , 20, by and between:

LANDLORD:   Janice Kay McCarty, a single woman, residing at 5511 Salem Hill Drive, Austin, Travis County, Texas 78745 (hereinafter "Landlord"); and

TENANT:   Thessalonian Mandate Institute, a Texas nonprofit corporation organized exclusively for religious purposes under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A), EIN 42-2419586, with its principal office in Austin, Travis County, Texas, acting through its Minister and Chief Executive, Rickey Jay Bennett, II (hereinafter "Tenant").

1. Premises

Landlord leases to Tenant, and Tenant leases from Landlord, the following described real property situated in Lee County, Texas (hereinafter "Premises"), together with all improvements, if any, located thereon:

Being a 0.924 acre tract of land situated in Lee County, Texas, being out of and a part of the Drew Champion Survey, Abstract No. 358, Lee County, Texas, more particularly described by metes and bounds as recorded at Volume 1335, Pages 705–707, Official Public Records of Lee County, Texas, and commonly known as 1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Texas 78942.
The Premises are leased in their current as-is condition, without functioning utility infrastructure including electrical power and water supply. The parties acknowledge that the Premises lack an operational well and solar power system at the commencement of this Lease, and that the monthly rent has been established to reflect the current as-is condition of the Premises.
2. Lease Term

This Lease shall commence on (hereinafter "Commencement Date") and shall continue on a month-to-month basis until terminated by either party upon thirty (30) days' written notice to the other party, or until superseded by the exercise of the Option to Purchase described in the separate Option Agreement of even date herewith.

3. Rent

Tenant shall pay Landlord a monthly rent of $ (hereinafter "Monthly Rent"), due and payable on the first (1st) day of each calendar month. Rent shall be paid by check, electronic transfer, or such other method as the parties may agree in writing. A grace period of five (5) days shall apply before any late charge is assessed.

The Monthly Rent has been established to reflect the current as-is condition of the Premises, including the absence of functioning utility infrastructure. The parties agree that this rent represents the fair market rental value of the Premises in their present unimproved condition.

4. Use of Premises

The Premises shall be used exclusively for the religious, ministerial, educational, and administrative purposes of the Thessalonian Mandate Institute, consistent with its mission as a faith-based organization under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A), and for use as the ministerial dwelling of its Minister as designated by the Board of Directors under 26 U.S.C. § 107. No use inconsistent with applicable law or the Tenant's religious mission shall be permitted.

5. Utilities and Infrastructure

Tenant shall be responsible for obtaining and paying for all utilities and services to the Premises. The parties acknowledge that the Premises currently lack functioning power and water supply infrastructure. Landlord and Tenant may jointly contribute to the installation and development of utility infrastructure, including solar power systems and water well development, on the terms set forth in Section 6 of this Lease.

6. Improvements and Improvement Ledger

During the term of this Lease, Landlord and Tenant may contribute funds toward capital improvements to the Premises, including but not limited to solar power installation, water well drilling and development, and related infrastructure. All such contributions shall be documented contemporaneously in an Improvement Ledger maintained by Tenant and approved by Landlord, identifying the date, amount, nature, and contributing party for each capital improvement expenditure.

The Improvement Ledger shall distinguish between (a) Landlord's contributions, which shall be treated as capital improvements increasing Landlord's cost basis in the Premises, and (b) Tenant's contributions, which shall constitute credits against the purchase price if and when Tenant exercises the Option to Purchase described in the separate Option Agreement of even date herewith.

Routine maintenance and repair expenditures shall not constitute capital improvements for purposes of this Section and shall not be credited against any future purchase price.

7. Maintenance and Repairs

Tenant shall maintain the Premises in good condition and shall be responsible for routine maintenance and minor repairs. Landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs and major systems repairs not caused by Tenant's negligence or misuse. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord of any condition requiring repair.

8. Assignment and Subletting

Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet the Premises or any portion thereof without the prior written consent of Landlord.

9. Default

If Tenant fails to pay rent when due and such failure continues for ten (10) days after written notice, or if Tenant materially breaches any other provision of this Lease and such breach continues for thirty (30) days after written notice, Landlord may terminate this Lease upon written notice to Tenant. Termination of this Lease shall not affect the separately executed Option Agreement unless the Option Agreement expressly provides otherwise.

10. Holdover

If Tenant remains in possession of the Premises after termination or expiration of this Lease without a new written agreement, such holdover shall be on a month-to-month basis at the same Monthly Rent, subject to termination upon thirty (30) days' written notice by either party.

11. Relationship to Option Agreement

This Lease and the Option Agreement executed by the parties on or about the same date are separate and independent instruments. Nothing in this Lease shall be construed to require Tenant to exercise the Option to Purchase, and nothing in the Option Agreement shall be construed to require Tenant to remain in occupancy under this Lease. The termination of this Lease shall not automatically terminate the Option Agreement unless expressly provided therein.

12. Governing Law

This Lease shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas. Venue for any dispute arising hereunder shall be in Lee County, Texas.

13. Entire Agreement

This Lease constitutes the entire agreement of the parties with respect to the leasing of the Premises and supersedes all prior negotiations and agreements. This Lease may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both parties.

14. Notices

All notices under this Lease shall be in writing and delivered by hand, certified mail, or electronic mail with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set forth above, or to such other address as a party may designate in writing.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Lease Agreement as of the date first written above.

Janice Kay McCarty — Landlord

Rickey Jay Bennett, II, Minister & Chief Executive
Thessalonian Mandate Institute — Tenant

Austin, Texas  ·  EIN 42-2419586  ·  26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A)
Lease Agreement
1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Lee County, Texas 78942

This Lease Agreement (hereinafter "Lease") is entered into as of the day of , 20, by and between:

LANDLORD:   Janice Kay McCarty, a single woman, residing at 5511 Salem Hill Drive, Austin, Travis County, Texas 78745 (hereinafter "Landlord"); and

TENANT:   Thessalonian Mandate Institute, a Texas nonprofit corporation organized exclusively for religious purposes under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A), EIN 42-2419586, with its principal office in Austin, Travis County, Texas, acting through its Minister and Chief Executive, Rickey Jay Bennett, II (hereinafter "Tenant").

1. Premises

Landlord leases to Tenant, and Tenant leases from Landlord, the following described real property situated in Lee County, Texas (hereinafter "Premises"), together with all improvements, if any, located thereon:

Being a 0.924 acre tract of land situated in Lee County, Texas, being out of and a part of the Drew Champion Survey, Abstract No. 358, Lee County, Texas, more particularly described by metes and bounds as recorded at Volume 1335, Pages 705–707, Official Public Records of Lee County, Texas, and commonly known as 1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Texas 78942.
The Premises are leased in their current as-is condition, without functioning utility infrastructure including electrical power and water supply. The parties acknowledge that the Premises lack an operational well and solar power system at the commencement of this Lease, and that the monthly rent has been established to reflect the current as-is condition of the Premises.
2. Lease Term

This Lease shall commence on (hereinafter "Commencement Date") and shall continue on a month-to-month basis until terminated by either party upon thirty (30) days' written notice to the other party, or until superseded by the exercise of the Option to Purchase described in the separate Option Agreement of even date herewith.

3. Rent

Tenant shall pay Landlord a monthly rent of $ (hereinafter "Monthly Rent"), due and payable on the first (1st) day of each calendar month. Rent shall be paid by check, electronic transfer, or such other method as the parties may agree in writing. A grace period of five (5) days shall apply before any late charge is assessed.

The Monthly Rent has been established to reflect the current as-is condition of the Premises, including the absence of functioning utility infrastructure. The parties agree that this rent represents the fair market rental value of the Premises in their present unimproved condition.

4. Use of Premises

The Premises shall be used exclusively for the religious, ministerial, educational, and administrative purposes of the Thessalonian Mandate Institute, consistent with its mission as a faith-based organization under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A), and for use as the ministerial dwelling of its Minister as designated by the Board of Directors under 26 U.S.C. § 107. No use inconsistent with applicable law or the Tenant's religious mission shall be permitted.

5. Utilities and Infrastructure

Tenant shall be responsible for obtaining and paying for all utilities and services to the Premises. The parties acknowledge that the Premises currently lack functioning power and water supply infrastructure. Landlord and Tenant may jointly contribute to the installation and development of utility infrastructure, including solar power systems and water well development, on the terms set forth in Section 6 of this Lease.

6. Improvements and Improvement Ledger

During the term of this Lease, Landlord and Tenant may contribute funds toward capital improvements to the Premises, including but not limited to solar power installation, water well drilling and development, and related infrastructure. All such contributions shall be documented contemporaneously in an Improvement Ledger maintained by Tenant and approved by Landlord, identifying the date, amount, nature, and contributing party for each capital improvement expenditure.

The Improvement Ledger shall distinguish between (a) Landlord's contributions, which shall be treated as capital improvements increasing Landlord's cost basis in the Premises, and (b) Tenant's contributions, which shall constitute credits against the purchase price if and when Tenant exercises the Option to Purchase described in the separate Option Agreement of even date herewith.

Routine maintenance and repair expenditures shall not constitute capital improvements for purposes of this Section and shall not be credited against any future purchase price.

7. Maintenance and Repairs

Tenant shall maintain the Premises in good condition and shall be responsible for routine maintenance and minor repairs. Landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs and major systems repairs not caused by Tenant's negligence or misuse. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord of any condition requiring repair.

8. Assignment and Subletting

Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet the Premises or any portion thereof without the prior written consent of Landlord.

9. Default

If Tenant fails to pay rent when due and such failure continues for ten (10) days after written notice, or if Tenant materially breaches any other provision of this Lease and such breach continues for thirty (30) days after written notice, Landlord may terminate this Lease upon written notice to Tenant. Termination of this Lease shall not affect the separately executed Option Agreement unless the Option Agreement expressly provides otherwise.

10. Holdover

If Tenant remains in possession of the Premises after termination or expiration of this Lease without a new written agreement, such holdover shall be on a month-to-month basis at the same Monthly Rent, subject to termination upon thirty (30) days' written notice by either party.

11. Relationship to Option Agreement

This Lease and the Option Agreement executed by the parties on or about the same date are separate and independent instruments. Nothing in this Lease shall be construed to require Tenant to exercise the Option to Purchase, and nothing in the Option Agreement shall be construed to require Tenant to remain in occupancy under this Lease. The termination of this Lease shall not automatically terminate the Option Agreement unless expressly provided therein.

12. Governing Law

This Lease shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas. Venue for any dispute arising hereunder shall be in Lee County, Texas.

13. Entire Agreement

This Lease constitutes the entire agreement of the parties with respect to the leasing of the Premises and supersedes all prior negotiations and agreements. This Lease may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both parties.

14. Notices

All notices under this Lease shall be in writing and delivered by hand, certified mail, or electronic mail with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set forth above, or to such other address as a party may designate in writing.

Option to Purchase Agreement
1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Lee County, Texas 78942
This Option to Purchase Agreement is a separate and independent instrument from the Lease Agreement executed by the parties on or about the same date. The existence of this Option does not obligate Optionee to purchase the Property, and the existence of the Lease does not obligate Optionor to sell.

This Option to Purchase Agreement (hereinafter "Option Agreement") is entered into as of the day of , 20, by and between:

OPTIONOR:   Janice Kay McCarty, a single woman, residing at 5511 Salem Hill Drive, Austin, Travis County, Texas 78745 (hereinafter "Optionor" or "Seller"); and

OPTIONEE:   Thessalonian Mandate Institute, a Texas nonprofit corporation organized exclusively for religious purposes under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A), EIN 42-2419586, with its principal office in Austin, Travis County, Texas, acting through its Minister and Chief Executive, Rickey Jay Bennett, II (hereinafter "Optionee" or "Buyer").

1. Grant of Option

In consideration of Ten Dollars ($10.00) and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Optionor hereby grants to Optionee the exclusive right and option to purchase (hereinafter "Option") the following described real property situated in Lee County, Texas (hereinafter "Property"):

Being a 0.924 acre tract of land situated in Lee County, Texas, being out of and a part of the Drew Champion Survey, Abstract No. 358, Lee County, Texas, more particularly described by metes and bounds as recorded at Volume 1335, Pages 705–707, Official Public Records of Lee County, Texas, and commonly known as 1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Texas 78942.
2. Option Period

This Option shall be effective as of the date first written above and shall remain in effect indefinitely until exercised or until terminated by mutual written agreement of the parties. There is no fixed expiration date for this Option. Optionee may exercise this Option at any time by delivering written notice of exercise to Optionor in accordance with Section 5 of this Agreement.

3. Purchase Price — Appraisal-Based Determination

The purchase price for the Property shall not be fixed at the time of execution of this Agreement. Upon Optionee's delivery of notice of exercise, the parties shall promptly engage a mutually agreed independent certified appraiser, licensed in the State of Texas, to determine the fair market value of the Property as of the date of exercise. The appraiser shall be agreed upon within fifteen (15) days of notice of exercise. If the parties cannot agree on an appraiser within fifteen (15) days, each party shall select one appraiser and those two appraisers shall jointly select a third, whose determination shall be binding.

The gross purchase price shall be the fair market value as determined by the appraisal. The net purchase price payable to Optionor shall be the gross purchase price reduced by any improvement credits as provided in Section 4 of this Agreement.

4. Improvement Credits

During the term of the Lease Agreement between the parties, Optionee may make capital improvements to the Property, including but not limited to solar power installation and water well development. All such capital expenditures by Optionee shall be documented in the Improvement Ledger maintained pursuant to the Lease Agreement.

Upon exercise of this Option, the documented total of Optionee's capital improvement contributions as reflected in the Improvement Ledger shall be credited against the gross purchase price as established by appraisal. This credit reflects the return to Optionee of its prior capital investment in the Property and shall not be construed as a reduction in the fair market value of the Property.

Purchase Price Formula
Appraised Fair Market Value at Date of Exercise
minus Documented Optionee Capital Improvement Credits (Improvement Ledger)
= Net Purchase Price Payable to Optionor

Optionor's contributions to capital improvements during the lease period shall not be credited against the purchase price but shall be reflected in Optionor's adjusted cost basis in the Property.

5. Exercise of Option

Optionee may exercise this Option at any time by delivering written notice to Optionor stating Optionee's intent to purchase the Property. Exercise of the Option shall be irrevocable upon delivery of such notice. Within five (5) business days of the appraisal being completed and the net purchase price determined, the parties shall execute a standard Texas Contract for Sale of Real Property consistent with the terms of this Agreement.

6. Closing

Closing shall occur within forty-five (45) days of the determination of the net purchase price, at a title company or attorney's office in Lee County, Texas, unless the parties agree in writing to an alternate location or date. At closing, Optionor shall deliver a General Warranty Deed conveying fee simple title to the Property to Optionee, free and clear of all liens and encumbrances except those of record as of the date of this Agreement and any created by Optionee during the lease period.

7. Title and Survey

Optionee shall have the right, at its expense, to obtain a current title commitment and survey of the Property prior to closing. Optionor shall cure any title defects that are not permitted exceptions within a reasonable time not to exceed thirty (30) days. If Optionor is unable to cure a material title defect within that period, Optionee may elect to terminate the purchase without penalty, and this Option shall remain in effect for future exercise.

8. Property Taxes

Property taxes for the year of closing shall be prorated as of the closing date. Following closing, Optionee shall apply for applicable religious organization property tax exemption from the Lee County Appraisal District under Texas Tax Code § 11.20.

9. No Obligation to Purchase

Nothing in this Agreement shall obligate Optionee to exercise this Option. Optionee's failure to exercise shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement or the Lease Agreement. The Option consideration paid is non-refundable regardless of whether the Option is exercised.

10. Governing Law

This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas. Venue for any dispute shall be in Lee County, Texas.

11. Entire Agreement

This Agreement, together with the Lease Agreement of even date, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties regarding the Option to purchase the Property. This Agreement may be amended only by written instrument signed by both parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Option Agreement as of the date first written above.

The Thessalonian Mandate Institute
Austin, Texas  ·  EIN 42-2419586  ·  26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A)
Board Resolution
Authorization of Lease Agreement and Option to Purchase Agreement
Action by Written Consent Without a Formal Meeting

Pursuant to Article IV, Section 4.10 of the Bylaws of the Thessalonian Mandate Institute, the undersigned, constituting the Board of Directors of the Institute, hereby adopts the following resolutions by written consent in lieu of a formal meeting, effective as of the date set forth below.

Date of Action:  

Recitals

WHEREAS, Thessalonian Mandate Institute (hereinafter "the Institute") desires to establish a permanent church seat and ministry facility in furtherance of its theological mission under 26 U.S.C. § 508(c)(1)(A);

WHEREAS, Janice Kay McCarty, a single woman unaffiliated with the governance or operations of the Institute, is the sole owner of approximately 0.924 acres of real property located at 1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Lee County, Texas 78942, being out of the Drew Champion Survey, Abstract No. 358 (hereinafter "the Property");

WHEREAS, Janice Kay McCarty has offered to lease the Property to the Institute and to grant the Institute an option to purchase the Property, and the Board has reviewed the terms of the proposed Lease Agreement and Option to Purchase Agreement;

WHEREAS, the Property is currently in an as-is condition without functioning utility infrastructure, and the proposed lease terms reflect the current unimproved condition of the Property;

WHEREAS, Janice Kay McCarty is not an officer, director, or substantial contributor of the Institute, and this transaction does not involve a disqualified person within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. § 4958;

WHEREAS, the Board has determined that entering into the Lease Agreement and Option to Purchase Agreement is in the best interest of the Institute and consistent with its theological mission;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

Resolutions
Resolution 1 — Authorization of Lease Agreement

RESOLVED, that the Institute is hereby authorized to enter into a Lease Agreement with Janice Kay McCarty for the lease of the Property located at 1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Lee County, Texas, on substantially the terms reviewed by the Board, and that the Minister and Chief Executive, Rickey Jay Bennett, II, is hereby authorized and directed to execute the Lease Agreement on behalf of the Institute and to take all actions necessary to carry it into effect.

Resolution 2 — Authorization of Option to Purchase Agreement

RESOLVED, that the Institute is hereby authorized to enter into an Option to Purchase Agreement with Janice Kay McCarty granting the Institute the right to purchase the Property at a price to be determined by independent appraisal at the time of exercise, with improvement credits as described therein, and that the Minister and Chief Executive is hereby authorized and directed to execute the Option to Purchase Agreement on behalf of the Institute.

Resolution 3 — Authorization of Capital Improvement Expenditures

RESOLVED, that the Minister is hereby authorized to expend Institute funds toward capital improvements to the Property during the lease term, including solar power installation and water well development, provided that all such expenditures are documented contemporaneously in the Capital Improvement Ledger maintained pursuant to the Lease Agreement, and that no single capital improvement expenditure exceeding $5,000 shall be made without prior Board notification.

Resolution 4 — Ministerial Housing Allowance Confirmation

RESOLVED, that the Board hereby confirms that the Property, once occupied by the Minister, is designated as the ministerial housing for Rickey Jay Bennett, II, consistent with Resolution 5 of the Founding Board Resolution dated May 5, 2026, and that the housing allowance designation previously made thereunder shall apply to the Property at 1032 Private Road 1339, Giddings, Texas.

Resolution 5 — Authorization to Apply for Property Tax Exemption

RESOLVED, that the Minister is hereby authorized to apply to the Lee County Appraisal District for religious organization property tax exemption under Texas Tax Code § 11.20 upon the Institute's occupancy of the Property, and to execute all documents and take all actions necessary to obtain and maintain such exemption.

Resolution 6 — Authorization to Exercise Option

RESOLVED, that when the Board determines it is in the best interest of the Institute to exercise the Option to Purchase, the Minister is hereby authorized to deliver notice of exercise, engage an independent appraiser, and execute all documents necessary to complete the purchase of the Property, subject to Board approval of the final net purchase price at the time of exercise.

Note on Governance: The Board has confirmed that Janice Kay McCarty, the Landlord and Optionor, has no role in the governance, operations, or finances of the Thessalonian Mandate Institute. This transaction is an arm's-length arrangement between the Institute and an unaffiliated third party. No conflict of interest exists and no recusal is required.
Certification

The undersigned, constituting the Board of Directors of the Thessalonian Mandate Institute, hereby certify that the foregoing resolutions were duly adopted by written consent in lieu of a meeting, that they constitute the valid and binding actions of the Board, and that this Resolution shall be filed with the permanent records of the Institute.

Rickey Jay Bennett, II — Founder, Minister, Director

## Frequently asked questions

**How much does Holdings cost?**

Start free with banking and invoicing. $25/mo for full accounting. $59/mo if you want us to close your books for you. Banking is included at every tier.

**Do I need to be good with numbers?**

No. The free plan gives you banking and invoicing — no accounting required. If you want to go deeper, the $25 plan walks you through it. And at $59, we handle everything for you.

**What are the free tools?**

57 free tools for invoices, tax estimates, budgets, P&L reports, expense tracking, nonprofit checklists, and more. Use them without an account. They’re included with every plan. [See all tools](https://getholdings.com/tools).

**Do I have to open a business account?**

Nope. Holdings works with your existing bank — we connect through Plaid. But if you add Holdings banking (free), your transactions flow in automatically and your balance earns 1.75% APY.

**Is my money safe?**

Yes. Deposits are held at i3 Bank, Member FDIC, insured up to $3M. We use 256-bit encryption and are SOC 1 and PCI DSS certified.

**What if I just want to try it?**

Start free — banking and invoicing at $0/mo, no credit card required. Upgrade to accounting or bookkeeping anytime. If it’s not for you, cancel anytime.

**Can I switch plans?**

Anytime. Upgrade, downgrade, or cancel in one click. Your data carries forward.

**How is this different from QuickBooks / Xero / Wave?**

Those are accounting software. Holdings is accounting + banking + tools + automation in one place. Depending on your plan, we either help you do it or do it for you. And our pricing starts way lower. [See comparisons](https://getholdings.com/compare).

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

# Settings
W, H = 1280, 720
FPS = 24
DURATION = 4  # seconds
FRAMES = FPS * DURATION

BG = (15, 26, 70)       # navy #0F1A46
GOLD = (184, 145, 42)   # gold
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
LGOLD = (220, 185, 90)  # lighter gold for URL

font_bold = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSerif-Bold.ttf"
font_reg = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSerif.ttf"
font_sans = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf"
font_sans_bold = "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf"

os.makedirs("/home/claude/card_frames", exist_ok=True)

def draw_frame(alpha):
    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

    def col(c):
        return tuple(int(v * alpha) for v in c)

    # TMI name - large
    f1 = ImageFont.truetype(font_bold, 54)
    name = "Thessalonian Mandate Institute"
    bbox = d.textbbox((0,0), name, font=f1)
    x = (W - (bbox[2]-bbox[0])) // 2
    d.text((x, 60), name, font=f1, fill=col(WHITE))

    # Line 1
    f2 = ImageFont.truetype(font_sans_bold, 34)
    line1 = "We won't just get you back to work."
    bbox = d.textbbox((0,0), line1, font=f2)
    x = (W - (bbox[2]-bbox[0])) // 2
    d.text((x, 190), line1, font=f2, fill=col(WHITE))

    # Line 2 - split gold highlight
    line2a = "You'll be the boss of the machine that took "
    line2b = "your job!"
    f3 = ImageFont.truetype(font_sans_bold, 34)
    bbox_a = d.textbbox((0,0), line2a + line2b, font=f3)
    total_w = bbox_a[2] - bbox_a[0]
    x_start = (W - total_w) // 2
    d.text((x_start, 240), line2a, font=f3, fill=col(WHITE))
    w_a = d.textbbox((0,0), line2a, font=f3)[2]
    d.text((x_start + w_a, 240), line2b, font=f3, fill=col(GOLD))

    # Line 3
    line3 = "Don't wait for the world to pass you by."
    bbox = d.textbbox((0,0), line3, font=f2)
    x = (W - (bbox[2]-bbox[0])) // 2
    d.text((x, 340), line3, font=f2, fill=col(WHITE))

    # Line 4 - gold highlights
    line4a = "Own it"
    line4b = " and "
    line4c = "control your future!"
    f4 = ImageFont.truetype(font_sans_bold, 34)
    full = line4a + line4b + line4c
    total_w = d.textbbox((0,0), full, font=f4)[2]
    x_start = (W - total_w) // 2
    d.text((x_start, 390), line4a, font=f4, fill=col(GOLD))
    w4a = d.textbbox((0,0), line4a, font=f4)[2]
    d.text((x_start + w4a, 390), line4b, font=f4, fill=col(WHITE))
    w4ab = d.textbbox((0,0), line4a + line4b, font=f4)[2]
    d.text((x_start + w4ab, 390), line4c, font=f4, fill=col(GOLD))

    # URL
    f5 = ImageFont.truetype(font_sans, 28)
    url = "thessalonian-mandate-institute.org"
    bbox = d.textbbox((0,0), url, font=f5)
    x = (W - (bbox[2]-bbox[0])) // 2
    d.text((x, 510), url, font=f5, fill=col(LGOLD))

    # Tagline
    f6 = ImageFont.truetype(font_reg, 24)
    tag = "The one who is willing to work shall be equipped to work."
    bbox = d.textbbox((0,0), tag, font=f6)
    x = (W - (bbox[2]-bbox[0])) // 2
    d.text((x, 620), tag, font=f6, fill=col(WHITE))

    return img

# Generate frames
# First 24 frames (1 sec): blank navy
# Next 48 frames (2 sec): fade in
# Last 24 frames (1 sec): full hold

for i in range(FRAMES):
    if i < 24:
        alpha = 0.0
    elif i < 72:
        alpha = (i - 24) / 48.0
    else:
        alpha = 1.0
    
    img = draw_frame(alpha)
    img.save(f"/home/claude/card_frames/f{i:04d}.png")

print("Frames done")
EOF
